_how_to_fill_this_in: One object per test case. A test case is one acceptance criterion from week02/requirements.json, turned into steps that anyone can follow and a result that anyone can check.

id: TC-NNN-NN. NNN is the number of the requirement it tests, and NN counts the test cases of that requirement: TC-004-01 and TC-004-02 both test REQ-004. As with the REQ ids, a test case id never changes its meaning. A test case you drop keeps its id and gets "dropped": true.
req: the REQ id it tests, exactly as in week02/requirements.json. One requirement per test case.
title: what is tested, in a few words, such as 'A wrong code is refused'.
precondition: what must be true before the first step, such as 'A code has been sent to deniz@example.com'. Write 'none' if nothing is needed.
steps: what the tester does, one action per line, with the real values to type: 'Enter deniz@example.com and tap Send code'. Someone who has never seen your project must be able to follow them.
expected: what the tester must see at the end, in one full sentence: a screen, a message, a number. Not 'it works', but 'The home screen opens and shows the three free rooms'.

Every must requirement has at least one test case. For at least three requirements, write a second test case for what happens when something goes wrong: a wrong code, an empty field, a slot that is already taken.

The three test cases below belong to the two requirements that everyone shares, REQ-001 and REQ-006. Keep them and adjust the wording to your screens. If your phone-screen requirement has another id, change the id and the req of TC-006-01 to match it (REQ-007 gives TC-007-01). Replace the fourth one with your own, and add as many as you need.
You may delete this block once you have read it; the checker ignores it.

test_cases.title: Log in with the correct verification code
test_cases.precondition: The prototype is open in a browser.
steps: Enter student@example.com in the e-mail field.
test_cases.expected: The home screen opens and no password is requested.

test_cases.title: A wrong verification code is refused
test_cases.expected: A wrong-code error message appears and the user remains on the code screen.

test_cases.title: Create a discussion post
steps: Enter 'Database Systems Exam' in the title field.
Enter 'Does anyone have revision notes for the exam?' in the post content field.
test_cases.expected: The browser navigates to post.html, as specified by the prototype form.

test_cases.title: A post cannot be submitted with an empty required field
steps: Select a category and enter some post content.
test_cases.expected: The browser's required-field validation prevents submission and keeps the user on the create-post screen.

test_cases.title: View a discussion and its replies
steps: Open the sample Database Systems discussion.
Read the discussion content and displayed replies.
test_cases.expected: The discussion page displays the sample post and its existing replies.

test_cases.title: Search for an available study resource
steps: Enter 'Java' in the resource search field.
test_cases.expected: The Java OOP resource remains visible and resources that do not match the search are filtered out.

test_cases.title: Display a message when no resources match
steps: Enter 'xyz-no-match-123' in the resource search field.
test_cases.expected: No resource cards remain visible and the no-results message is displayed.

test_cases.title: View a student profile
test_cases.expected: The profile screen displays the sample student's courses, skills, and areas of expertise.
